before.exam_tip_html: When a question asks you to explain targeting or marketing techniques, name the specific technique, explain how it works, and then link it to the assumptions the producer is making about their target audience. The examiner wants to see that you understand the relationship between audience profiling and the marketing choices made — not just a description of what a trailer is.

When applying Jenkins’ convergence theory in an extended response, do not simply say “convergence means everything is on one device.” The strongest answers distinguish between technological convergence (devices and platforms merging) and cultural convergence (audiences engaging across platforms as active participants), then show how a specific media product or industry illustrates both dimensions. Examiners reward the distinction between the two levels of convergence.

When a question asks you to ‘analyse the codes and conventions’ of a media product, the examiner wants you to name and apply specific codes (not just say ‘the lighting is dark’ but ‘the low-key lighting, a technical code, connotes danger and moral ambiguity’). For genre questions, always name the genre, identify at least two conventions, and consider whether the product conforms to or subverts them. Mentioning Steve Neale’s argument about repetition and difference will lift a genre answer into the higher bands if the theory is actually applied to the product rather than just summarised.
